questions.scenario: Consider the binary tree diagram provided below with various nodes labelled. The root is labelled as A, and it has two children B and C. Node B has two children D and E, while node C has two children F and G. Node D has two children H and I, and node E has one child J. questions.question: Calculate the depth of the tree, defined as the length of the longest path from the root to a leaf node.
marking_criteria: Identify the longest path from root to a leaf node
Count the number of edges in the longest path
hints: Stay focused on this: Calculate the depth of the tree, defined as the length of the longest path from the root to a leaf node — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Provide the final answer.
questions.model_answer:
The longest path from the root A is A -> B -> D -> I or A -> B -> D -> H. Both paths have a length of 3 edges.

3
questions.explanation: The depth of the tree is determined by finding the longest path from the root node to a leaf node. The longest path in this tree is from the root A to the leaf nodes I or H, which each have a path length of 3 edges.

questions.scenario: Consider the binary tree diagram provided below with various nodes labelled. The root is labelled as A, and it has two children B and C. questions.question: Explain why the nodes D, H, and I form a sub-tree. What is the significance of the parent node in this context?
marking_criteria: Identify the parent node of H and I
Explain the significance of the parent node D in this context
hints: Answer every labelled part of the question, and link your points so a marker can follow the full argument.
questions.model_answer:
Nodes D, H, and I form a sub-tree because D is the parent node of H and I. A sub-tree is a subset of nodes and edges of a tree where the root of the subset is connected to the rest of the tree through a single parent node. In this case, node D is the parent node of H and I, making them a sub-tree.

D is the parent node, and H and I are child nodes forming a sub-tree.
questions.explanation: A sub-tree is a subset of nodes and edges in a tree where the root of the subset is connected to the rest of the tree through a single parent node. In this tree, node D is the parent node of nodes H and I, making them a sub-tree.

questions.scenario: You are analysing the data transfer rates of two multimedia streaming applications over a 10 Mbps network.
questions.question: Find the data transfer rate for Application D, given that it transfers 250 MB in 100 seconds.
marking_criteria: Correctly calculating the data transfer rate
hints: Stay focused on this: Find the data transfer rate for Application D, given that it transfers 250 MB in 100 seconds — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Including the unit; Providing the final answer.
questions.model_answer: Data Transfer Rate = (250 MB / 100 s) * 8 = 2 MB/s * 8 = 16 Mbps.
questions.explanation: Calculate the data transfer rate using the provided formula and convert to Mbps.

hints: Stay focused on this: Explain the consequence of Application E having a data transfer rate of 8 Mbps over a 10 Mbps network — develop the idea fully rather than listing short points. Make sure you also cover: Logical explanation; of relevant concepts.
questions.model_answer: If Application E has a data transfer rate of 8 Mbps over a 10 Mbps network, it means that the application is utilizing 80% of the network's capacity. This could result in sufficient performance without overwhelming the network, but it also means there is room for other applications to use the remaining 2 Mbps without issues.
questions.explanation: Explain the impact of the data transfer rate on network capacity and application performance.
